**Reading.**

1. *At the default nothing changes.* `off` is WP-57's grid to the number in all 29 rows (44 given up — 24 crossing pairs on 16 halted entrants, 10 sliding, 9 brake distance, 1 crawling; 14 honest by WP-55's count — 5,988 exits of 6,131 reached, 14 lane-1 minutes at or below 5 m/s, 5,439 deferred, 218 pair releases, 45 unfinished, the entrances 5,944, no collision), the T.H.52 capacity rows read 395 / 401 / 373 of 466 against the 420 pinned, the no-lock pin passes at seeds 3–5, and golden `merge_weave` is byte-identical (hash 436cd4ec9e5d; not regenerated). The key's clock runs at the default (the trace above reads it) and never drops.
2. *The rule does what it was derived to do, and the hold it cuts is the ramp queue's.* At 2 s it drops 8,330 holds on 4,265 changers; 5,653 of the drops are of an entrant still on the ramp, at 7.2 m/s median, 1,168 of an entrant on the section, 1,509 of an exiter, 45 under the exit priority. The follower released is never inside its brake gap (the clock does not run there), and no form collides (0 in 308 fixture runs). Where the stall is long at the default — the ramp queue, 36 of the 40 longest — the rule cuts it at the bound.
3. *And it reads worse, in every form, by the same mechanism.* H2: give-ups 44 → 74, exits 5,988 → 5,897 of 6,131 → 6,084 reached, lane-1 minutes at or below 5 m/s 14 → 31, forced changes 529 → 709, deferred 5,439 → 9,407, pair releases 218 → 458, the entrances 5,944 → 5,830, the exiters' mean wait 10.2 → 11.1 s. H1 70, H4 59, H2sec 59 (74 unfinished, 13,257 deferred), H2np 80 (the entrances 5,749, the worst), D40 66 (the entrances 5,948, the best, and still two pinned seeds broken), S2 64. Row by row the sign is consistent, not a re-roll's coin: the given-ups are worse on 9–16 rows and better on 4–7 in every form (H2 9 / 7 / 12 equal; H1 16 / 6; D40 13 / 6), the forced deferrals rise on 13–19 rows. The mechanism is in the last table: **a changer released at speed parity meets the next follower at the same speed and stalls again** — the stall's own condition (F's side open, the changer not closing on L) holds for the next gap as for the last, because the changer is slow relative to lane 1 and not because of which follower is behind it — so 1,118 changers are released three times or more at 2 s (2,603 at 1 s, 132 at 4 s), and **the entrants reach the section with a gap 79 % → 62 % of the time** (41 % in H2sec, where the ramp's accumulated clock drops the hold on the first section step). An entrant arriving with no gap is the state the second attempt built the ramp anticipation against (a through vehicle at 28.7 m/s meeting an entrant appearing at 19 m/s 7 m ahead of it); on the section it hands its change to the forced mode at the lane end, and the deferrals, the pair releases and the pairs at the lane ends follow. The honest give-ups barely move (no move at `b`: 14 → 14–23), the "no entrant ahead" class carries the rise (26 → 35–59: sliding past 10 → 17–33, crawling 1 → 1–10).
4. *The no-lock pin breaks in every form.* The T.H.52 capacity fixture at seed 5 under H2 stands lane 1 at the section start at 0.4 and 0.5 m/s over t = 600–720 s (5.1 m/s the minute before, back to 6.1 m/s only at t = 1,080–1,140 s), 288 of 466 departed against 373, 10 exits given up, 257 pair releases; H2np the same two minutes (0.4 and 0.5 m/s, 299 departed), onH2 the same two (0.5 and 0.8 m/s, 299 departed). Every other form fails the pin on `n_missed` (2–9 against 1) or the 80 % entrance at one of the two pinned seeds or both (the table above); `off` and `on` pass it at seeds 3–5. None of these is a permanent lock (no row stays at a standstill to the end, no collision), but a rule that breaks the fixture's no-lock pin cannot ship, and it is the kind of transient that VM M's corridor made permanent.
5. *One worsened row traced: the sequence moves, the pair does not.* Ruth St corridor fleet, exit peak, seed 4: 1 → 10 given up under H2, five of them (t = 254.5–310.5 s) beside v00954, an entrant that reached the section at 20.5 m/s (`b` 1.98) with no gap in both runs and was never released itself; at `off` it changes at 2.4 m/s with 9.8 m of lane left, under H2 it halts with 1.1 m left and the next five exiters are given up beside it. The run had diverged from `off` from t = 64 s through six ramp releases (v00944 … v00955, the last at t = 242.0 s: v00955 at 15.7 m/s released from v00173 at 19.2). That row is the platoon re-sequenced, as the WP-55..57 rows were; what is not a re-roll is the sign over the grid (item 3) and the one variable every form moves the same way — the entrants arriving without a gap.
6. *Time and distance.* The distance form D40 binds later at low speed, as derived (4,279 drops against 8,330, the drop after 40 m of travel ≈ 4.7 s at the long stalls' 8.6 m/s and 13 s at 3 m/s), and reads between H2 and H4 (66 given up, 5,948 entrants) — no better than the time forms on the pairs, and it breaks the pin at seeds 4 and 5. The strict stall S2 (the deficit not shrinking at all) fires on 1,249 holds, the fewest, and still reads 64 given up with the pin broken at seed 4 (9 missed, 367 departed). The exit priority's holds are not what costs: exempting them (H2np, 8,652 drops) reads worse than H2 (80 against 74) — at the default they are 2 % of the held steps and 78 steps past the 2 s mark.
7. *With the exiter's yield on the bound does not make it safe.* `on` reproduces WP-56's rows (39 given up, 6,015 exits, the entrances 5,973, 89 exiter-yield vehicle-steps; the pin passes at seeds 3–5). onH2 reads 66 given up with the pin broken at seed 5 (lane 1 0.5 m/s, 299 departed) and 44 yield steps; onS2 63 with the pin broken at seed 4 and 103 yield steps. Two things to be plain about: the fixtures never reproduced VM M's lock (the yield on passes every pin here), so the grid cannot show the yield made safe; and VM M's 18,259 steps are `n_exiter_yields` — the exiter's own yield command (`_weave_yield_at_ends`), which this bound does not touch (it bounds the follower's hold in `_weave_cooperate`). The bound is therefore **not** a candidate for a corridor battery with the yield on.
8. *The golden with the key set* moves (hash 955b8ba08cc6 at 2 s; 9 holds dropped on `weave.osm`; mean travel time 69.500 → 69.538 s, p90 84.126 → 86.847, σ_v 3.940 → 4.009, 15 / 18 / 2 / 6 against 14 / 19 / 2 / 6); at the default it does not.

**Nothing ships.** `WEAVE_DEFAULTS["hold_release_s"]` = 0: hash-neutral unless set, the fixture grid at the default is WP-57's to the byte, golden `merge_weave` unchanged (hash 436cd4ec9e5d, `test_golden_summary_reproduced[merge_weave]` passes), the T.H.52 tests' markers and pins unchanged. The rule stays as a measured option with its counter and its clock, so a corridor battery can read where it would bind. For the record, as in WP-56 and WP-57: any rule of this series that ships on must pass a 20-seed VM corridor battery before it stays on — VM M's lesson — and this package ran no corridor.

**What this hands on.** The hold trace changes the target. The unbounded hold is, by held steps, first of all the ramp's anticipation (53 %; 36 of the 40 longest stalls): an entrant in the ramp queue chooses its lane-1 gap up to `lookahead_m` (120 m) before the section and holds that gap's follower at the queue's speed, 3–10 m/s, for up to 43 s — a lane-1 throttle at the ramp queue's speed, upstream of the section. Bounding its duration does not help, because the positioning is what the hold buys and a changer released at parity meets the next follower at the same speed. The lead left is not to start that hold before it is needed: gate the ramp anticipation's *cooperation* (not its gap choice or easing) by the entrant's time to the section start against the follower's time to open the gap at `b` — a queued entrant 100 m out at 5 m/s (20 s) gets no follower yet, while the 19 m/s arrival the second attempt derived the anticipation for (≈ 6 s out) keeps it — to be measured against the second attempt's trace (the 28.7 m/s through vehicle meeting a 19 m/s entrant 7 m ahead) and the T.H.52 entrance rows, with this package's hold trace as the baseline. Separately, the exiter's yield's own bound (WP-56's (a): the standstill lapse inside the zone, or a cap on yields per halted entrant) remains the path for `exiter_yields` to return, since VM M's steps are that command's; the fixtures cannot show it safe, only a VM battery can.

## 2026-09-24 (block 3, WP-60, the gated anticipation): the ramp's follower held only once the entrant's arrival needs it — the ramp holds go, the entrants reach the section without their gap, and every criterion reads worse; nothing ships (`anticipation_gate` = 0)

**Why.** The owner's block-3 item 1 is the weaving section at capacity: `test_th52_weave_at_capacity_flows` (strict `xfail`) departs 395 / 401 / 373 of 466 entrants at seeds 3 / 4 / 5 against the 420 pinned, and lane 1's first 60 m past the gore reads 3.9 / 4.3 / 3.3 m/s at its minimum, at or below 5 m/s in 2 / 5 / 4 of the 18 windows. WP-58's hold trace (above, reproduced to the number in this package's `off` grid) put the unbounded hold first of all on the ramp: 109,904 of the 206,358 held changer-steps (53 %) are an entrant still on the ramp at a median 5.7 m/s, and 36 of the 40 longest stalls (22.5–43 s) are ramp-queue entrants holding a lane-1 follower at their own speed — upstream of, and into, the 60 m the capacity test reads. WP-58's lead: do not bound the hold, do not start it before it is needed — gate only the ramp anticipation's *follower cooperation* (not its gap choice, not its easing) by the entrant's time to the section start against the time the follower needs to open the gap at its own `b`. That is what this package derives and measures. The ramp throttle, the demand, every scenario and every other rule are untouched.

**The derivation (`microsim.runner._weave_coop_gate`, called from `_weave_cooperate` for the approaching entrants, which now pass their `arrival_s`; `WEAVE_DEFAULTS["anticipation_gate"]`, 0 = off).** Project the entrant onto lane 1 (its front at `x_c`, speed `v_c`, held constant — the constant-speed extrapolation of the easing check, `_weave_easing_ok`) and take the follower F of its chosen gap behind it: the gap `s_f = x_c − len_c − x_F`, the closing speed `Δv = v_F − v_c`. The acceptance asks of the follower side the time gap at F's speed, `s_need = s0_c + accept_gap_s · v_F` (F's current speed, the largest it has over the manoeuvre), so the deficit now is `D = s_need − s_f` (negative when open). F braking at `b_F` from now holds the gap `s(τ) = s_f − Δv·τ + b_F·τ²/2`: it closes at the closing speed, and braking for `τ` opens `b_F·τ²/2` against holding the speed. The time F needs to open the gap is when `s(τ)` is back at `s_need`, the positive root of `b_F·τ²/2 − Δv·τ − D = 0`:

    t_open = (Δv + √(Δv² + 2·b_F·D)) / b_F

With `Δv² + 2·b_F·D < 0` — `s_f − Δv²/(2·b_F) > s_need`, F can shed its closing speed at `b_F` and still keep the accepted gap — braking at `b_F` never lets the gap fall short and nothing is needed yet; with `D ≤ 0` and `Δv ≤ 0` the root is at most 0 (open and opening). The speed-aware guard's brake gap is inside the root: under braking at `b_F` the gap left once the closing speed is shed, `s(τ) − (Δv − b_F·τ)²/(2·b_F) = s_f − Δv²/(2·b_F)`, is invariant, so the discriminant's sign is that term's test. The acceptance's IDM absorption term is F's own model and has no closed form; the section's cooperation (ungated) finishes what the gate starts late. **The rule:** an approaching entrant's follower is commanded (IDM towards the entrant, clipped at `−b_F`, as before) from the first step on which the root is real and the entrant's time to the section start, `arrival_s = (x_start − x_c)/max(v_c, 3 m/s)`, is no longer than it, and from then on while it stays the chosen follower (`gate_f` in the changer's hold state: the gate decides when the hold starts, not whether it continues); before that F keeps its own car-following. A follower that passes the entrant's projection before the gate opens is never held behind it. The vehicle-steps on which the gate withholds a command that would have bound (below F's own model) are counted in `n_anticipation_gated` — the **38th `weave_sections` key** (docs/CONTRACTS.md §2, `WeaveSectionDiagnosticsOut`, `WEAVE_FIELDS`). A switch, not a fitted value.

Worked at constant speeds and 0.5-s steps (`b_F` 1.67 m/s², `s0` 2 m, `accept` 0.6 s; session script, the runner's function): the queued entrant 100 m out at 5 m/s (20 s) with a follower at 10 m/s 20 m behind its projected rear reads `D` = −12 m and a discriminant of −15, no hold; F reaches the projected rear 4 s later, when its root is 7.3 s against the entrant's 16 s — never held. The arrival the anticipation was built for (the second attempt's trace: a through vehicle at 28.7 m/s meeting an entrant appearing at 19 m/s 7 m ahead of it) opens the gate with F 44 m behind, 3.8 s before the arrival (ungated, the hold starts at the zone's entry, 6.3 s out); braking at `b_F` F arrives at 22.3 m/s 19.2 m behind and settles 15.8 m behind at the entrant's speed (13.4 m asked there), 2.0 s into the section.

**Measured** on the same 29-run grid as WP-51..58 (seeds 3 / 4 / 5 on the Ruth St module at both demand points and both fleets, the Ruth St corridor fleet at the 271.4 m window, the T.H.52 corridor-demand and capacity fixtures, the two two-entrance fixtures, the moderate fixture and the golden; 20 simulated minutes at step 0.5 s, macOS, about a minute of wall-clock per grid, run one at a time), the exiter's yield off (the default). WP-58's harness with three additions (session record): a `GATE` line per (entrant, follower) reading of the gate, an `ARRIVE` line per entrant — its first section step (speed, the lane-1 follower's and leader's gap and speed at that step, the gap chosen on the ramp) and its change (section metres driven, forced, the zone reached, halted), including the entrants SUMO's own model moves to lane 1 in the step they reach the section, which the weave never drives — and the key passed as its own argument to every run. Variants: `off`, the default (identical to WP-58's `off` in all 29 rows, every counter and the golden's metrics compared); **GL, the rule as derived** (`anticipation_gate` = 1); G (harness), the gate re-read every step with no latch — the first form written; GLT (harness), the deficit read at the fleet's desired headway `T` = 1.4 s instead of the acceptance's 0.6 s (the gate opens earlier); NF (harness), the anticipation's follower never commanded — the gate never open, the bound of what gating can do. Binding vehicle-steps are `n_anticipation_gated`.

**Reading.**

1. *At the default nothing changes.* `off` is WP-58's grid to the number in all 29 rows (44 given up — 24 crossing pairs on 16 halted entrants, 10 sliding, 9 brake distance, 1 crawling; 14 with no move at `b` — 5,988 exits of 6,131 reached, 5,439 deferred, 218 pair releases, 45 unfinished, the entrances 5,944, no collision), the hold trace is WP-58's (206,358 held changer-steps, 53 % on the ramp at 5.7 m/s, 36 of the 40 longest stalls ramp holds), the T.H.52 capacity rows read 395 / 401 / 373 of 466, the no-lock pin passes at seeds 3–5, and golden `merge_weave` is byte-identical (hash 436cd4ec9e5d; not regenerated).
2. *The gate does what it was derived to do.* The held steps on ramp entrants fall from 109,904 to 13,142 (53 % → 10 %), the 40 longest stalls are no longer the ramp queue's (36 → 11 of them ramp holds, the longest 43.0 → 33.5 s), and the gate opens on 13 % of its (entrant, follower) readings, a median 3.1 s before the entrant reaches the section; the readings that never open were first made a median 20.2 s out at 3.7 m/s — the queued entrant the lead described. The latched form does not collide (0 in 28 runs).
3. *And it reads worse on every criterion, by one mechanism: the entrants reach the section without their gap.* GL against `off`: give-ups 44 → 58 (crossing pairs 24 → 36 on 16 → 21 halted entrants, no move at `b` 14 → 24), exits 5,988 → 5,782 of 6,131 → 5,950 reached, lane-1 minutes at or below 5 m/s at the gore's end 14 → 31 and at the T.H.52 section start 15 → 42, forced changes deferred 5,439 → 10,549, pair releases 218 → 680, unfinished 45 → 62, the entrances 5,944 → 5,415 (E1 1,444 → 1,463). The T.H.52 entrance is lower on all 12 T.H.52 and two-entrance rows, the lane-1 minutes worse on 14 rows and better on 2, the give-ups worse on 10 and better on 6 — the entrance is not a re-roll. The arrival table says why: 62 % of the entrants the gate reads reach the section with no follower held, the lane-1 follower meets the acceptance's time gap at the arrival for 53 % of all entrants against 78 % (40 % against 71 % at T.H.52 capacity), SUMO's own model moves 947 of them to lane 1 in the arrival step against 1,580, and the change comes a median 16 m into the section instead of at its first metre. The hold does not go away; it moves onto the section, where it is shorter and harsher — held steps on entrants on the section 31,444 → 48,223, on exiters 60,904 → 68,752, 26,812 episodes against 17,810 — and there it is lane 1 at the section start that pays, at the resolution of the abreast pairs the early hold used to prevent (abreast at the arrival 991 → 1,474 over the grid). At T.H.52 capacity the ramp queue's arrival speed falls from 7.0 to 4.8 m/s at the median: an entrant that dwells on the auxiliary lane holds the ramp behind it, so the insertion falls. **The early hold is the positioning the entrant arrives with, not only a throttle**: WP-58 read its length as the cost; this package reads what the length buys.
4. *The capacity test.* It fails at every seed with the rule as without it, and worse: lane 1's first 60 m at or below 5 m/s in 6 / 14 / 9 of 18 windows against 2 / 5 / 4, the entrance 379 / 315 / 343 against 395 / 401 / 373 (419.4 asked); `n_missed` reads 1 at every seed either way (the test asks 0), unfinished 7 / 7 / 7 against 4 / 2 / 3 (10 % allowed), no collision. The no-lock pin breaks at seeds 4 and 5 on the entrance (315 and 343 against 372.8), the lane-1 floor of 2 m/s holds.
5. *The case the anticipation exists for is kept.* The second attempt's signature — a lane-1 follower at least 5 m/s faster than the entrant inside the acceptance's time gap at the arrival — reads 1 at `off`, 0 under GL and 63 without any anticipation follower (21 of them fast arrivals); in the second attempt's own window (T.H.52 capacity, seed 3, t ≤ 60 s) no fast arrival reaches the zone under GL, against two arriving abreast and a 205 m drive under NF. What the fast arrivals lose under GL is the congestion of everyone else: reached the zone 14.4 → 20.0 %, halted 14 → 49, forced 68 → 107 over the grid (NF 28.8 %, 51, 157).
6. *The forms around it.* Without the latch (G) the gate lets F go as soon as F has slowed enough and holds it again a step later; it reads as GL (60 given up, 5,426 entrants, the T.H.52 rows 380 / 325 / 350) and collides twice, both on the two-entrance fixture with the fleet defaults (seeds 3 and 4, t = 534.0 s and 479.5 s, lane 2 of the section at 55 m and 218 m): an exit-bound vehicle at 21.9 / 18.2 m/s executes its accepted change from lane 3 into lane 2 under mode 256 in the same step as a lane-1 vehicle the weave does not drive, at 5.2 / 7.6 m/s, moves into lane 2 by SUMO's own model, and the exiter lands 0.8 / 0.7 m behind it — a simultaneous-change conflict the weave's acceptance cannot see (it reads the target lane before SUMO executes the other changes of the step), met here because a slower lane 1 sends its vehicles into lane 2 beside the exiters; it is recorded, not fixed. With the deficit read at the fleet's desired headway (GLT: the hold starts earlier) the T.H.52 rows are mixed (377 / 364 / 382 at capacity, 431 / 372 / 399 at the corridor's demand) but the Ruth St corridor fleet's exit peak at seed 3 locks (lane 1 at the gore's end at 0.0 m/s in all 18 windows, 18,144 deferred, 21 unfinished, 42 of 73 entrants departed). Without any anticipation follower (NF) 60 given up, 5,303 entrants, 890 pair releases. Across GL, G and NF the direction is one: the less lead the ramp's hold has, the worse the section.
7. *Where the fixtures congest first — the corridor's question.* VM O's per-lane counts (docs/ONBOARDING_MNDOT.md §11) read the corridor's T.H.52 weave restricted first at its downstream end, the auxiliary lane and lane 1 before the exit, with the standstill head upstream of the gore forming later. The fixtures do not reproduce that. On both T.H.52 fixtures at the default the section's first 50 m of lanes 0 and 1 falls below 8 m/s at minute 2 in all six runs, the exit end at the same minute only at capacity seed 3 and later (minutes 4–18) or never elsewhere; below 5 m/s the entry cell goes at minute 2–3 (14 / 16 at the corridor's demand, seed 4), lane 1's exit end at the same minute only at capacity seed 3, at minute 5 at capacity seed 5, at 18 and 4 at the corridor's demand, seeds 3 and 5, and never at seed 4 of either. Lane 1's lowest minute over the last 60 m reads 4.7 / 10.7 / 5.0 m/s at capacity (3.8 / 11.9 / 1.7 at the corridor's demand) against 3.9 / 4.3 / 3.3 over the first 60 m (3.7 / 4.4 / 3.7). Lane 1 is the least-used of the four lanes at x = 290 m only at capacity seeds 4 and 5 (286 and 295 vehicles); elsewhere the auxiliary lane is. So the capacity fixture — and its test's lane-1 criterion — is an entry-end fixture: it measures where entrants and the lane-1 cooperation meet, not the exit end the corridor restricts first. The gate moves the entry onset earlier (below 8 m/s from minute 1 in five of six runs; below 5 m/s at the corridor's demand, seed 4, from minute 4 instead of 14) and does not move the exit end consistently (at capacity below 5 m/s in lane 1 from minute 2 → never at seed 3, never → 6 at seed 4, 5 → 8 at seed 5).

**Nothing ships.** `WEAVE_DEFAULTS["anticipation_gate"]` = 0: hash-neutral unless set, the fixture grid at the default is WP-58's to the byte, golden `merge_weave` unchanged (hash 436cd4ec9e5d, `test_golden_summary_reproduced[merge_weave]` passes), the T.H.52 tests' markers and pins unchanged (the strict `xfail` of `test_th52_weave_at_capacity_flows` stays; the rule does not make it pass at any seed). The rule stays as a measured option with its counter, so a corridor battery can read where it would bind. As for every rule of this series: any rule that ships on must pass a 20-seed VM corridor battery before it stays on (VM M's lesson); this package ran no corridor, and on the fixtures this one would not reach one.

**What this hands on.** Two readings change. (a) *The ramp hold is not the lane-1 throttle WP-58 took it for.* Its length is what positions the entrant: cut the lead time and the entrants arrive beside platoons, the hold moves onto the section at `−b`, and lane 1 at the section start — where the capacity test reads — gets slower, not faster. Every form that shortens it (WP-58's seven releases, this gate in four forms) reads worse, so the next derivation should leave the anticipation's lead alone and, if the ramp queue's speed is the cost to be cut, act on the queue's speed itself rather than on the follower waiting for it. (b) *The capacity fixture is an entry-end fixture, and the corridor restricts first at the exit end.* The owner's item 1 as pinned (lane 1's first 60 m, the entrance count) cannot show a derivation aimed at the corridor's restriction; the fixture that can is one that reproduces VM O's reading — the auxiliary lane and lane 1 slowing before the exit first — and its exit side (on these fixtures the exit link drains freely, as the first derivation noted). The lead, in order: build or re-parameterise a T.H.52 fixture judged at the exit end (lane 1 and the auxiliary lane over the last 60 m, per-lane counts at the gore's end) until it congests there first, as the corridor does; derive against that; keep the capacity test as the entry-end regression it is. Separately, the simultaneous-change collision of G (an exiter's mode-256 change into a lane another vehicle enters by SUMO's model in the same step) is a latent defect of the acceptance that a slower lane 1 exposes; it did not fire at the default in any run here.

## 2026-09-24 (block 3, WP-61, the corridor's section as a test): the T.H.52 section as the corridor compiles it, under the observed 05:30–05:50 movements — the auxiliary lane at the gore's end slows first and the approach's lane 0 breaks down after it, the corridor's order; the section takes 3,830–3,970 of the 4,820 veh/h offered; a strict-`xfail` free-flow test

**Why.** The owner's block-3 item 1 is the weaving section at capacity: a failing test, then a re-derivation. WP-60 (above) found both T.H.52 fixtures congest first at the section's entry end while VM O (docs/ONBOARDING_MNDOT.md §11) read the corridor's weave restricted first at its exit end, and handed on a fixture judged at the exit end; WP-59 (same §11) put the corridor capacity-short at this weave, not demand-high — the real section took S790's 3,776 plus T.H.52's 1,361 = 5,137 veh/h at 05:40 in free flow. This package builds that fixture from committed files only, measures where it congests first, and writes the failing test at the observed demand. The runner, the config schema, every scenario and every existing test assertion are untouched.

**The section as built.** The corridor scenario (`scenarios/mndot_i94_wb_stpaul_weave.yaml`: `data/osm/mndot_i94_wb_stpaul.osm` with `--ramps.guess --ramps.ramp-length 250 --ramps.unset 1001426896` and the connection patch `data/osm/mndot_i94_wb_stpaul.splits.con.xml`) was compiled by `osm_import` exactly as `run_micro` compiles it (session script; netconvert only, no simulation). The weave edge 51388891 starts at x = 10,426.6 m and is 305.0 m long (the OSM way measures 304.6 m). The demand artifact's ramp positions — on-ramp 769818012 at 10,329.5 m, off-ramp 18207598 at 10,721.6 m, the "392 m" — are those of a compile without ramp guessing: compiled that way, the same edge starts at 10,329.5 m and is 392.2 m long (checked the same way). The section as run is 305 m, and VM O's positions are the run's x: 10.45 km is 23.4 m into the section, 10.70 km 273.4 m, 31.6 m before its end.

Reading. (1) *VM O's saturation reproduced on a 2-km fixture.* The section carries 3,828–3,966 veh/h at each of its three cross-sections (20-minute means over the seeds) against 4,822 veh/h offered on average (the four windows' flow into the weave) — 3,732–4,284 per window from minute 5, where VM O read 3,804–4,968 per window and 3,967–4,026 an hour on the corridor. Lane 1 is the least used of the four at the exit end (522–603 veh/h), as at the corridor's 10.70 km (669–715 vehicles in the hour); the approach's lane 0 is where the queue stands (VM N's head, 10.20–10.35 km, lane 0). At the constant 05:40 flows the three cross-sections carry 3,612–3,891 veh/h against 5,137. (2) *The precursor is the exit movement's.* In minute 2 the auxiliary lane's last 55 m holds mainline exiters (196 / 200 / 191 samples at 2 Hz) and entrants bound for the same exit (73 / 51 / 90) at 7.0–13.2 m/s; through entrants still owing their change are absent (0 / 4 / 0), while lane 1 beside them holds mainline exiters waiting to cross at 4.6 / 9.8 / 5.2 m/s. Mainline exiters that first reach lane 0 in the section's last 67 m: 27 of 262 / 44 of 295 / 66 of 305 — 8 / 20 / 27 of the 25 / 52 / 68 that reach the gore from the approach's lane 1 (two changes inside the section; median first lane-0 position 137 / 182 / 198 m) against 19 / 23 / 38 of the 237 / 238 / 235 from the approach's lane 0 (median 30.8 / 30.4 / 35.4 m). The exit end's lane 0 delivers 1,035–1,122 veh/h (20-minute means) where the four windows ask 1,267–1,484 veh/h of exits (the share times the flow into the weave; mean 1,405), crossing at 11.6–16.1 m/s — neither free flow nor a queue discharging at a lane's capacity (the fleet's straight-road capacity is 1,670–1,676 veh/h per lane, §11), which points at the rate at which exiters get into the lane rather than at the lane's own discharge.

**The test (`TestWeaveRun.test_th52_corridor_section_carries_free_flow_demand`, strict `xfail`; seed 3; 2.8 s locally).** The real section carried these flows in free flow: S790 ran 25.8–26.6 m/s and S97 26.8–27.4 m/s in all four windows, and no station of the corridor fell under 20 m/s before 06:30 (§11, "Where the corridor's queue comes from", (5)). Each criterion comes from that observation; the tolerances are allowances, not fits.

| criterion | from the observation | seed 3 | seed 4 | seed 5 |

| (i) ≥ 95 % of planned vehicles depart on the mainline | S790 passed its count | 1,140 of 1,196 (95.3 %) ✓ | 1,157 (96.7 %) ✓ | 1,149 (96.1 %) ✓ |
| (i) ≥ 95 % of planned vehicles depart on the T.H.52 entrance | rnd_91040 passed its count | 368 of 407 (90.4 %) ✗ | 360 (88.5 %) ✗ | 350 (86.0 %) ✗ |
| (ii) every lane's mean speed over the section's last 60 m above 20 m/s in every 5-min window (16 lane-windows) | the observation's aggregation, and the boundary §11 dates the corridor's queues with; the stations either side read 5.8 m/s or more above it | 10 of 16 at or below: lane 0 10.1–13.9, lane 1 12.9–16.7, lane 2 17.1 and 18.7 ✗ | 11: lane 0 11.9–15.7, lane 1 15.1–18.3, lanes 2–3 in three ✗ | 13: lane 0 9.2–12.9, lane 1 8.2–16.2, lanes 2–3 in five ✗ |
| (iii) no collision | — | 0 ✓ | 0 ✓ | 0 ✓ |
| (iv) exits given up (`n_missed_exit`) ≤ 2 % of the exit-bound vehicles that reach the section | the exit share is the conservation closure of counts every exiter left by | 2 of 356 ✓ | 1 of 391 ✓ | 2 of 405 ✓ |

The observation has no per-lane or in-section speed; 20 m/s is its station-level boundary applied per lane, the strict reading. It does not fail a free-flowing auxiliary lane slowing for the ramp's 22.22 m/s: the model's lane 0 at the exit end reads 21.3–21.7 m/s at the corridor's 10.70 km in minutes 0–5 (VM O) and 21.5–22.0 m/s over the section's last 55 m in the fixture's first minute. The xfail reason carries the seeds' values; the margins (86–90 % against 95 %, 8–16 m/s against 20) are far from the line, so the platform sensitivity of the CI note should not turn it into an XPASS. `test_th52_corridor_demand_is_the_observation` (not marked, instant) pins the demand constants to the committed observation and demand artifact, the two exit shares to the conservation closure, and the premise S790, S97 > 25 m/s in all four windows. The capacity test stays as the entry-end regression it is, and the 05:40-constant run above is a record, not a test.

**What this hands on.** The first derivation to try against the new test is on the exit movement's entry into the auxiliary lane, not on the entrance. At the corridor's own flows the section's first slowdown is the auxiliary lane at the gore's end filled with exiters (through entrants are not there), fed at 1,035–1,122 veh/h where 1,267–1,484 are due, with the exiters that arrive from the approach's lane 1 two and a half to four times as likely to reach lane 0 only in the last 67 m (32–40 % against 8–16 %) and those waiting in lane 1 at 4.6–9.8 m/s — the lane that then carries the least and whose feeder, the approach's lane 0, is where the queue stands. The candidate: exit-bound vehicles prepared upstream — asked into the approach's lane 0 inside the existing vacate window, the vacate rule's mirror for the exit movement — so that they arrive beside the auxiliary lane and change in the section's first half; judged by this test's exit-end speeds and the T.H.52 count, with the capacity test as the entry-end guard (it loads the approach's lane 0, the breakdown's own lane) and a 20-seed corridor battery before any default flips (VM M's lesson). Before trusting the transfer, the corridor itself should say how its exiters arrive: the fixture's 829 m approach with round-robin insertion puts 10–23 % of the mainline exiters one lane or more further left at the gore, the corridor's share is unmeasured (a VM O-style count of the lane at 10.30 km by route, from a first-hour run with trajectories kept).

Session artifacts (the node-fitting generator, the A3 variant fixture, the measurement and diagnostic scripts, the twelve runs) not committed; every number above is from those runs or from the committed files named.

## 2026-09-24 (block 3, WP-62, exiters to the right early): the vacate rule's mirror for the exit movement — in free flow the lane-change model has already put the exiters in the rightmost lane, in the queue the move finds no gap or joins the queue, and what it adds it adds to the lane both movements cross; the corridor section test reads no better in any of six forms; nothing ships (`exit_prepare` = 0)

**Why.** WP-61 (above) wrote the failing test the owner's block-3 item 1 asks for — `test_th52_corridor_section_carries_free_flow_demand` (strict `xfail`): the corridor's T.H.52 section as compiled, under the observed 05:30–05:50 movements on the corridor's fleet, departs 368 / 360 / 350 of 407 T.H.52 entrants at seeds 3 / 4 / 5 against the 387 asked, and 10 / 11 / 13 of the 16 lane-windows over the section's last 60 m read at or below 20 m/s — and handed on its first derivation: how exiters get into the auxiliary lane. The exit end's lane 0 delivers 1,035–1,122 veh/h where 1,267–1,484 are due, and the mainline exiters that arrive from the approach's lane 1 reach lane 0 only in the last 67 m 32–40 % of the time (8–16 % from the approach's lane 0). The candidate: the vacate rule's mirror — exit-bound vehicles inside the vacate window asked into the approach's rightmost lane, the one feeding section lane 1, under the vacate rule's safety terms, bounded, no chain, never against the vehicle's route, and not deadlocking against the vacate rule's own opposite move. This package derives it, measures it in six forms on the test's fixture and on the 29-run grid of WP-51..60, and reads WP-61's exit-movement readings before and after. The demand, every scenario, every fixture and every existing assertion are untouched.

**The geometry, and the rule derived from it (`microsim.runner._weave_exit_prepare_step`, `_weave_exit_prepare_abreast`; `WEAVE_DEFAULTS["exit_prepare"]`, 0 = off).**

*Why the rightmost approach lane.* Section lane 0 begins at the entrance's gore and leads only to the exit (the connections `_check_weave_pairs` validates); section lanes 1–3 continue the approach's lanes 0–2. The one lane from which a single change reaches the auxiliary lane is section lane 1, and the one lane feeding it on each corridor edge before the section is the lane the vacate rule empties of through traffic: `_weave_vacate_lanes` already walks it upstream edge by edge from netconvert's connections as `k_from` (with `k_to` feeding section lane 2), so an acceleration lane on the right shifts it and the rule follows. An exiter arriving in section lane `k` owes `k` changes inside the section, each through lane 1, which the entering movement crosses the other way; the HCM 7th ed. ch. 13 ramp weave counts one change per exiter (`LC_FR` = 1) on the premise that the exiters approach in the lane next to the auxiliary lane. The rule asks for that premise.

*How far ahead.* The window is the vacate rule's own, `vacate_ahead_m` = 500 m measured along the chain (its default's argument, the MUTCD advance guide sign half a mile out, holds for both movements). The move is one or two changes. At the approach's free-flow speed (17–24 m/s at 10.30 km in minutes 0–5, WP-61) SUMO's safety check asks of the target lane roughly the IDM gap `s0 + v·T` on each side plus a length — 2 × (2.53 + 21 × 1.32) + 5 ≈ 66 m, 3.1 s at 21 m/s, with the corridor fleet's population means — so the 500 m window holds seven or eight such changes and the HCM's 500-ft (150 m) influence area two, too few for a vehicle two lanes out that finds no gap at once; the 150 m window is measured beside the default (W). The lane-change model already looks this far: a probe of `vehicle.getBestLanes` on the fixture (seed 3, t = 60–120 s, session script) gives an exiter on the approach's lane 1 a best-lane offset of −1 with 534 m of continuation (to the section's end), one on lane 2 an offset of −2, and on the insertion edge's lane 1 an offset of −1 with 1,134 m; with `lcStrategic` 5 the corridor fleet's strategic lookahead covers the whole window. The rule's request under mode 512 is that strategic change made mandatory, with the model's own other changes off.

*At what rate the target lane can absorb them.* On the approach, the full sort — every mainline exiter in the rightmost lane, the through traffic in the other two — is within the fleet's straight-road capacity (1,670–1,676 veh/h per lane, docs/ONBOARDING_MNDOT.md §11) in every observed window: exiters 1,086 / 1,075 / 1,091 / 942 veh/h at 05:30 / 05:35 / 05:40 / 05:45 (the exit share times S790), through 1,098 / 1,246 / 1,343 / 1,405 veh/h per lane. The vacate rule's bound — `VACATE_LANE_CAPACITY_VEH_H` (2,050) less the flow the target lane carries into the window — is the rule's bound too (`_weave_vacate_bound_veh_h(..., "prep_flow_s")`, over the sightings of `k_from`), but a flow reading cannot tell the two branches of the fundamental diagram apart: the approach's rightmost lane queued at 2.2–3.1 m/s carries 540–768 veh/h (WP-61's 10.30 km readings, minutes 10–20) and reads as 1,280–1,510 veh/h spare. The fleet's equilibrium flow (IDM at the population means T 1.322 s and s0 2.53 m, 5 m vehicles, the 24.59 m/s limit; session script) peaks at 1,856 veh/h at 15.0 m/s; below that speed an added vehicle lowers the lane's flow. The derived reading of "can absorb" is therefore the target lane's branch, measured as the free-flow gate (F: an exiter asked only while the target lane around it, 50 m behind to 100 m ahead, averages 15 m/s or more). In the section the constraint is different: lane 1 is also the entrants' target lane. With every exiter in it and the crossing entrants entering it before the exiters leave — the fixture's order: the entrants first leave lane 0 a median 8–20 m into the section, the exiters first enter it 40–51 m in (below) — lane 1 over the section's first metres would carry 1,091 + 968 = 2,059 veh/h at 05:40 (968 = the 71.1 % of the 1,361 entrants that cross), more than a lane. The full sort is feasible on the approach and infeasible at the section's entry unless the two movements exchange one for one; an exiter arriving in lane 2 enters lane 1 downstream of the entrants, in effect metered.

*The rule.* Each vehicle bound for the paired exit (`exiting_ids`, not given up) on a window edge within `vacate_ahead_m` of the section start, in a lane left of `k_from`, is asked into `k_from`, nearest the section first, under the vacate rule's form (`vacate_no_follower_braking`): at 0 (the default form) once, `changeLane(k_from, duration)` under mode 512 (SUMO's safety check on both gaps, speed adaptation, every model change off) for the travel time to the section start floored at the creep speed, re-addressed across window edges, SUMO moving a vehicle two lanes out one lane at a time; at 1, one lane right per accepting step under mode 768, the gap read by `_weave_vacate_gap_ok` with, new, the changer's brake gap on the target lane's leader (`brake_lead`: this target lane is the slower one). Bounded by `vacate_max_veh_h` or the spare capacity above. Handed back — mode restored, an open request ended by a one-step stay, since on the section's edge the index `k_from` is the auxiliary lane — when seen in `k_from` on a window edge or in section lane 1 (`n_exit_prepared`, the **39th `weave_sections` key**: docs/CONTRACTS.md §2, `WeaveSectionDiagnosticsOut`, `WEAVE_FIELDS`), or on reaching the section still left of it; the hand-back runs before the section takes the vehicle under control, so the mode the section records is the vehicle's own. No chain: nobody else is commanded, each exiter is asked once, never while another scripted hold is on it (the vacate rule's guard, modes 512 / 256 / 768), and no request outlives the window. State-only counts (asked, reached the section still left, never asked, yielded, held vehicle-steps) are kept for a harness.

*The ordering against the vacate rule.* The two rules' vehicles are disjoint (the vacate rule never asks a vehicle bound for the paired exit, `vacate_exempt_ids`) but their moves are opposite, each into the other's source lane. The first form written left the ordering to SUMO — the vacate rule runs first each step, SUMO's lane changer processes vehicles front first — and SUMO does not order such a pair: each, under mode 512, refuses on the other and adapts its speed towards it. Traced on the grid (N below) such pairs stood for up to 82 s. So the vacate request goes first: an exiter one lane left of `k_from` abreast of a vacate-held through vehicle in `k_from` (`_weave_exit_prepare_abreast`: the two overlapping along the axis) is not asked while the pair lasts, and one already asked has its open request ended by a one-step stay and re-issued for the rest of its life once clear. The through vehicle then meets a vehicle keeping its lane, which SUMO's own gap logic resolves, and the vacate rule's behaviour is unchanged. Why the vacate first: its through vehicle is the one emptying the slot the exiter wants; the exit movement has the section's forced zone and priority as its last resort, the vacate move has none; and it keeps the default rule byte-identical wherever the two never meet. The gap-conditioned form needs no such step — a vehicle beside the changer refuses its gap.

**Measured.** Session harness `wp62_harness.py` (WP-60's, traces off, with `wp62_patch.py`: the variants, an opposing-pair trace — a vacate-held through vehicle in `k_from` and a rule-held exiter in `k_to` overlapping on a window edge, each asking into the other's lane — and the state-only counts in each row), grid script `grid62.sh` (the same 29 runs as WP-51..60: seeds 3 / 4 / 5 on the Ruth St module at both demand points and both fleets, the Ruth St corridor fleet at the 271.4 m window, the T.H.52 corridor-demand and capacity fixtures, the two two-entrance fixtures, the moderate fixture, the golden; 20 simulated minutes at step 0.5 s, macOS, one grid at a time), and `wp62_corr.py`: the corridor section test's body with the key set in a copy of its call (the strict marker untouched), at seeds 3 / 4 / 5, with WP-61's readings (per-lane crossings at VM O's positions, the mainline exiters' lane at the window start, at 10.30 km, 5 m into the section and at 10.717 km, where each first reaches the auxiliary lane, the crossing entrants' first lane-1 position, each lane's load by movement along the section). Forms: `off`, the default; **the rule** (`exit_prepare` = 1, with its ordering); N (harness), the rule without the ordering — the first form written; G (harness), the gap-conditioned form for this rule alone, the vacate rule in its default form; F (harness), the free-flow gate at 15 m/s; W (harness), this rule's window 150 m, the vacate rule's 500 m. A bug found by a unit test on the way — the target listing included section lane 1 only when some window vehicle stood in `k_from`, so an exiter that changed and crossed onto the section in one step was counted refused — was fixed and every grid and corridor run re-made; the default form's commands were the same either way and all 29 rows of every grid came out identical, counters included.

**Reading.**

1. *At the default nothing changes.* The `off` grid is WP-60's `off` to the number in all 29 rows (44 given up, 5,988 exits of 6,131 reached, the entrances 5,944, E1 1,444, 5,439 deferred, 218 pair releases, 45 unfinished, no collision), golden `merge_weave` byte-identical (hash 436cd4ec9e5d, not regenerated), and the corridor section runs are WP-61's (368 / 360 / 350 T.H.52 entrants; 10 / 11 / 13 lane-windows; the exit end's lane 0 1,035 / 1,104 / 1,122 veh/h; 27 / 44 / 66 exiters late).
2. *The corridor section test reads no better, in any form.* The rule binds — 71 / 95 / 95 exiters moved into the rightmost lane before the section, 88 / 146 / 152 asked, 2,261–4,528 held vehicle-steps — and the deliveries do not rise where it binds: the exit end's lane 0 carries 1,044 / 1,080 / 1,089 veh/h against 1,035 / 1,104 / 1,122, the T.H.52 entrance 371 / 355 / 337 against 368 / 360 / 350 (387 asked), the lane-windows at or below 20 m/s 11 / 10 / 14 against 10 / 11 / 13, and the mainline, which passed at every seed, fails at seeds 4 and 5 (1,105 and 1,116 of 1,196 against the 1,137 asked). The late exiters rise, 27 / 44 / 66 → 35 / 52 / 75, and the rise is the approach's lane 0's own (19 / 23 / 38 → 28 / 29 / 42), not the lane-1 arrivals it was aimed at (8 / 20 / 27 → 6 / 22 / 26). No form passes criterion (i) or (ii) at any seed; no form collides on this fixture. The best T.H.52 reading, G's 370 / 368 / 366, comes from 7 / 17 / 35 exiters moved, while F moves 10–16 and shifts the entrance by −4 / −23 / −23: rows moved by a few vehicles are the sequence re-rolled, as WP-56 read them.
3. *Why: in free flow the exiters are already there.* In minutes 0–5, 73 of 73, 77 of 78 and 77 of 81 of the mainline exiters crossing 10.30 km are in the rightmost lane at the default — SUMO's own strategic change (`lcStrategic` 5, the best-lane offset of −1 over the whole window) sorts them before the rule would ask. The approach's left lanes carry exiters only once the rightmost lane queues (14–36 per 5-min window in minutes 10–20), and there the rule's request meets the same lane with no gap: 16 / 50 / 54 of the exiters it asks reach the section still left of it. Between the window's start and 10.30 km SUMO's own model moves 30 / 24 / 33 exiters from lane 1 to lane 0 at the default; with the rule 42 / 37 / 52. At 10.30 km the rightmost lane's share goes 89 / 78 / 76 % → 90 / 77 / 76 %.
4. *And what it adds, it adds to the lane both movements cross.* The exiters it does move join the queue in the approach's rightmost lane and reach section lane 1 at its entry, where the entrants are arriving (lane 1 at +10 m: exiters 517 / 533 / 565 → 562 / 546 / 581 veh/h beside 236–385 crossing entrants); the lane-0-origin exiters then reach the auxiliary lane later. That is the derivation's section constraint read off the fixture: the entrants leave lane 0 first (median 7–17 m under the rule, 8–20 m at the default), the exiters enter it after (38–54 m), and an exiter arriving in lane 2 is metered into lane 1 downstream of them; moving it right early pushes against the section's own order rather than relieving it.
5. *The ordering is needed, and it is enough to remove what it was for.* Without it (N): 270 opposing pairs on the grid, 193 lasting 2 s or more, the longest 82 s — two vehicles standing abreast in a stopped queue on the insertion edge of the T.H.52 corridor-demand fixture, seed 5 (t = 453.5–535.0 s, x ≈ 98 m, both requests open for 84 and 161 s more); in another pair of that run the through vehicle stayed at 0 m/s while its own leader drew 76 m ahead (t = 355–360 s), held by its mode-512 speed adaptation towards the exiter beside it, and moved off at 363 s — a hold one rule's request makes of the other's. N also collides once, on the T.H.52 capacity fixture at seed 5 (t = 751.5 s, section lane 2, 14 m in): exiter v00779, whose request had expired at 735.0 s still two lanes out, reached section lane 3 at 13.6 m/s, and its accepted mode-256 change into lane 2 at 750.0 s executed in the same step as the undriven through vehicle v01714 moving from lane 1 into lane 2 by SUMO's own model at 3.2 m/s; the exiter landed 8.3 m (front to front) behind it at 13.1 m/s and hit it a second later — the simultaneous-change defect WP-60 recorded under its G, exposed by the re-sequencing, not commanded by the rule. With the ordering: no opposing pair, no collision on the grid, and a better grid than N's (given up 45 against 48, deferred 5,384 against 8,320, pair releases 233 against 351, lane-1 minutes at or below 5 m/s at the gore's end 17 against 21).
6. *The grid under the rule.* Given up 44 → 45, exits 5,988 → 5,973 of 6,131 → 6,136 reached, the entrances 5,944 → 5,847 (lower on 8 of the 12 T.H.52 and two-entrance rows), E1 1,444 → 1,476, lane-1 minutes at or below 5 m/s at the gore's end 14 → 17 and at the T.H.52 section start 15 → 12, forced changes deferred 5,439 → 5,384, pair releases 218 → 233, unfinished 45 → 47, no collision; it binds on 1,959 exiters over the 28 runs (2,845 asked, 835 reaching the section still left, 103,658 held vehicle-steps). The T.H.52 capacity fixture departs 373 / 382 / 401 of 466 against 395 / 401 / 373 and its no-lock pin fails on `n_missed` at seeds 3 and 5 (4 and 3 against at most 1). Golden `merge_weave` with the key set moves 10 exiters (hash f66e721d5b87, mean travel time 69.500 → 68.542 s, throughput 1,680.0 → 1,718.2 veh/h).
7. *The other forms.* G, the gap-conditioned form, asks on 8,483 steps and moves 670: it takes the exiters it holds out of their own strategic change (mode 768 turns every model change off) and offers them only gaps that need no follower braking, so 841 reach the section still left, and the grid reads worst of all — 102 given up, lane-1 minutes at or below 5 m/s at the gore's end 32, 8,731 deferred, and 229 pairs of a held exiter abreast of a vacate-held through vehicle (up to 38.5 s; the ordering's suspension is the default form's). F, the free-flow gate, moves 871 and reads like the rule on the grid (47 given up, the entrances 5,930, 61 unfinished) and worse on the corridor section (T.H.52 364 / 337 / 327, 11 / 11 / 14 lane-windows). W, the 150 m window, asks 2,141 exiters and moves 852 (1,270 reach the section still left) and gives the grid's best reading — 39 given up, the entrances 6,028 (8 rows up, 4 down, −27 to +38), the T.H.52 section start at or below 5 m/s in 4 minutes against 15, the no-lock pin passing at all three seeds (416 / 389 / 411) — and reads worse on the corridor section (the mainline 1,108 at seed 5, T.H.52 352 / 336 at seeds 4 / 5, the exit end's lane 0 1,023 / 1,080 / 1,092). W's grid rows are the entry-end fixtures, where it holds exiters under mode 512 over the approach's last 150 m in rows where it binds on 37–70 each; whether that is more than a re-roll would take a 20-seed battery, and it fails the judge this package was set.
8. *The corridor's arrival against the fixture's (VM P).* The fixture's approach does not reproduce the corridor's split. At 10.30 km the fixture's exiters are 76–89 % in the rightmost lane against the corridor's 55–68 %, and 0–4 % in the left lane against 1–15 %; 5 m into the section 59–68 % are in lane 1 and 9–23 % in lane 2 against 45–53 % and 26–39 %; they reach the auxiliary lane earlier (a median 254–265 m before the section's end against 231–239 m), fewer of them in the last 67 m (10–22 % against 21–25 %), and in the last 15 m both have 94–100 % in it. The fixture's exiters are inserted 829 m before the gore, inside the strategic lookahead from their first metre, and in free flow they are sorted before 10.30 km; the corridor's come over 10 km and its split holds in minutes 0–15 as in 15–60 (VM P), so on the corridor the left-lane exiters are not only the queue's. The corridor has more for the rule to act on than the fixture has in free flow. The fixture says two things that transfer: where the rightmost lane is queued the move finds no gap, and where it moves an exiter it adds it to lane 1 at the section's entry. Yet the fixture saturates at the corridor's rate (WP-61: 3,828–3,966 veh/h) with its exiters further right than the corridor's, which is itself evidence that the arrival split is not what caps the section.

**Nothing ships.** `WEAVE_DEFAULTS["exit_prepare"]` = 0: hash-neutral unless set, the fixture grid at the default is WP-60's to the byte, golden `merge_weave` unchanged (hash 436cd4ec9e5d), the T.H.52 tests' markers and pins unchanged; the strict `xfail` of `test_th52_corridor_section_carries_free_flow_demand` stays, the rule making it pass at no seed in any form. The shipping condition — the corridor section test's criteria improved by mechanism, binding where the deliveries rise, no lock, no collision, the grid's entrance rows and the capacity test not worse — is met by no form: the rule binds and the exit end's lane-0 delivery does not rise, the mainline criterion breaks at two seeds, the entrances fall and the no-lock pin breaks at seed 5. The rule stays as a measured option with its counter, its ordering and its unit tests, so a corridor battery can set it.

**What this hands on.** (a) *The exit end's deficit is not the approach's arrival split.* On the fixture the split is already the one the candidate asked for in free flow, the section slows first at its exit end all the same (WP-61), and the late exiters rise when more exiters arrive in section lane 1. The next derivation belongs inside the section, on the order of the crossing: the entrants leave the auxiliary lane in its first 8–20 m while the exiters enter it 40–51 m in, both through section lane 1, and lane 1 at the entry cannot carry the full exiter flow and the crossing entrants at once (2,059 veh/h at 05:40 against a lane's 1,670). An exchange that pairs an exiter's change into the auxiliary lane with the entrant's change out of it — the exiter taking the slot the entrant leaves, where the section's acceptance now reads the two changes separately — is where a rule could raise the exit end's lane-0 delivery; it should be judged by this test's exit-end windows and the lane-0 delivery, with the T.H.52 count and the capacity fixture's no-lock pin as the guards. (b) *The fixture's approach under-represents the corridor's left-lane exiters* (VM P: a third to two fifths one or two lanes out at 10.30 km, from the first minutes). Any approach-side rule should be read on an approach that delivers the corridor's split, or on the corridor itself: a 20-seed battery with `exit_prepare` = 1 is cheap (the key exists) and would say whether the corridor's free-flow left-lane exiters respond where the fixture's queued ones cannot; this package does not claim they would. (c) *The latent simultaneous-change defect* (WP-60's G, here N's collision): an exiter's accepted mode-256 change into a lane that an undriven vehicle enters by SUMO's own model in the same step. It fired at no default run here; a rule that re-sequences the section exposes it.

## 2026-09-25 (block 3, WP-64, the swap): an entrant and an exiter that block each other exchange lanes in one step — SUMO executes the pair when it does not overlap, the rule binds 44–45 times a run and completes every exchange, but the pairs that block each other overlap near speed parity at the entry, and no criterion of the corridor section test improves; nothing ships (`swap_pairs` = 0)

**Why.** The owner's block-3 item 1 is the weaving section at capacity: a failing test, then a re-derivation. The failing test is WP-61's `test_th52_corridor_section_carries_free_flow_demand` (strict `xfail`): at the observed 05:30–05:50 movements the corridor's T.H.52 section departs 368 / 360 / 350 of 407 T.H.52 entrants at seeds 3 / 4 / 5 (387 asked) and 10 / 11 / 13 of the 16 lane-windows over its last 60 m read at or below 20 m/s. WP-62 (above) found that pre-positioning the exiters on the approach does not help and named the deficit as the crossing order inside the section: the entrants leave the auxiliary lane (section lane 0) a median 8–20 m in, the exiters enter it 40–51 m in, both through section lane 1. Its hand-on: pair an exiter's change in with an entrant's change out, the exiter taking the place the entrant leaves, so the two movements share lane 1 instead of each needing its own gap; judged by the corridor section test's exit-end windows and lane-0 delivery, with the T.H.52 count and the capacity fixture's no-lock pin as guards. This package derives that exchange, probes how SUMO executes it, measures it on the test's fixture and on the 29-run grid of WP-51..62, and records a guard for the latent simultaneous-change defect of WP-60 and WP-62. The demand, every scenario, every fixture and every existing assertion are untouched.

**What SUMO does with such a pair (probed first; SUMO 1.27.1, libsumo, a straight 2,000 m edge of two or three lanes, IDM, 5 m vehicles, `minGap` 2.5 m, 10 m/s, step 0.5 s; session scripts `wp64/swapprobe*.py`).**

1. *An overlapping pair is never exchanged.* Two vehicles abreast in lanes 0 and 1, each asked into the other's lane in the same step: with their fronts level, 3 m apart and 6 m apart (1 m between bumpers) neither changes, under mode 256 or 512, and both adapt their speed towards the other (10 → 9.2 m/s in the step). With lengths 5 / 7 m or speeds 10 / 12 m/s, fronts level: the same.
2. *A pair that does not overlap is exchanged in one step under mode 256.* With the fronts 7.6, 8, 10 or 15 m apart (2.6 m or more between bumpers, more than the rear's `minGap`) both requests execute in the one step, whichever lane is in front, no collision; at 7.5 m exactly one orientation executes and the other does not (the floating-point edge of "reported gap ≥ 0"). Asked alone, either vehicle changes at those offsets too: mode 256 refuses an overlap and nothing else. The rear 2 m/s faster at 8 m: neither changes (the gap after the step's move, 2 m, is under the `minGap`); the rear 2 m/s slower: both. Under mode 512 neither changes at any offset up to 15 m (SUMO's own secure gap).
3. *SUMO executes a step's changes front vehicle first, across lanes.* A in lane 0 asked left, B in lane 2 asked right, both into lane 1, 3 m between bumpers: with B in front under 256 and A under 512, B changes and A is refused; with B in front under 512 and A under 256 both change and A lands 3.0 m behind B's rear (0.5 m reported) at 10 m/s; with A in front the front one changes first in every combination and a rear one under 512 is refused. So a mode-256 change is refused only on an overlap, including an overlap with a vehicle that entered its target lane earlier in the same step, and lands at any smaller gap behind it — the latent defect of WP-60 (G) and WP-62 (N), where an exiter's mode-256 change landed just behind a vehicle that had entered the same lane from the other side in the same step.
4. *SUMO does not announce a model change a step ahead.* A keep-right change on an empty road executed at t = 6.0 s with `vehicle.getLaneChangeState(v, −1)` (SUMO's saved state) reading no bits before that step and the step before it: an undriven vehicle's change cannot be read before it happens.

**The derivation (`microsim.runner._weave_swap_step`, `_weave_swap_offset_ok`, `_weave_swap_opposing_clear`, `_weave_change_ok`; `WEAVE_DEFAULTS["swap_pairs"]`, 0 = off).**

*The pair.* A driven entrant E in section lane 0 (owing its change left) and a driven exiter X in section lane 1 (owing its change right). R is the one whose front is behind (ties by id), P the other; `d` the bumper offset from R's front to P's rear, negative while they overlap. They are a pair when they are each other's nearest vehicle across — nobody in P's lane between P and R's front, nobody in R's lane between R and P's front — and at least one change is refused by the section's acceptance because of the other: R with P as its leader, or P with R as its follower (`_weave_change_ok`, the acceptance of `_weave_step` restated for supplied gaps: the leader side at `_weave_lead_gap_min`, the follower side at the time gap and the follower absorbing the changer at its `b`, and the forced guard with both brake gaps). The distance that defines "near-abreast" is therefore the acceptance's own: overlapping, or nearer than `s0 + accept · v` plus a `minGap` between bumpers (8.0 m at 5 m/s with 2.5 m `minGap`s and 0.6 s).

*Each is the other's natural gap.* After an exchange R stands in P's lane behind P's old place and P in R's lane ahead of R's old place. R's new leader is P's leader, its follower P's follower Q, at `g_PQ − d − len_R`; P's new leader is R's leader, at `g_R,L − d − len_P`, its follower R's follower, farther than before. Against the partner the exchange asks nothing: the two end in different lanes. What it asks of each lane is one length plus the offset on one side — behind P in P's lane, ahead of R in R's lane. Against two separate changes that is a saving of exactly the partner's time gap: at car-following spacing (reported `T · v`, the corridor fleet's population means in `artifacts/idm_i24_capacity.json`, `T` 1.322 s and `s0` 2.53 m, 5 m vehicles, `accept` 0.6 s, `d` at the parity guard below) a separate change needs a gap 12.0 m larger than the lane has at 5 m/s and 11.4 m at 10 m/s, the exchange 9.0 m and 5.4 m in each of the two lanes; the exchange fits into car-following spacing unopened only from 17.4 m/s (session arithmetic). At queue speeds the saving is a quarter of the cost; the rest — a length and the `minGap`s of two vehicles that cannot overlap — is physical.

*Against the partner, the forced guard.* SUMO executes the pair front first (probe 3), and if it refuses one of the two — an overlap with a vehicle that entered the target lane earlier in the step — the pair is left in one lane, R behind P at `d`. So the two changes are read against each other by the forced guard, the weave's own minimum for any change (`_weave_force_gap_ok`): R onto P as its leader and P in front of R as its follower, the reported gap `d − s0_R` on either side (`_weave_swap_offset_ok`). Both reduce to `d − s0_R > max(s0_R, s0_P)` plus the closing terms of a faster R — its accepted time gap over the closing speed and its brake gap at `b_R` — so a pair at speed parity needs one `minGap` of each between bumpers (5.0 m; from fronts level, 10 m), a rear 2 m/s faster 6.2 m, and the one left behind in a half-executed exchange is never the faster. This is also which of the two moves "first": neither movement is privileged; the one in front is executed first because SUMO does so, and the closing terms make the rear the slower one or level, so where one lane is slower its vehicle is the rear. On the corridor section the pairs form at near parity (below), so neither lane is systematically the rear: E is in front in 17 / 19 / 13 of the 44 / 45 / 44 exchanges at seeds 3 / 4 / 5.

*Against everyone else, the full acceptance, with the partner removed.* (ii) R's change in P's lane: leader P's leader, follower Q; (iii) P's change in R's lane: leader R's leader, follower R's follower. The exchange is thus the acceptance minus the partner, and a pair of which SUMO executes only one change is left at a forced-guard gap, the faster in front.

*The guard against two opposing changes into one lane (iv), `_weave_swap_opposing_clear`.* From probe 3: a mode-256 change is unsafe exactly when a vehicle processed before it (ahead of it) has entered its target lane from the other side in the same step. The exchange's two changes enter different lanes (E into lane 1, X into lane 0), each the lane the other leaves, so the pair never meets itself. X enters lane 0, which only lane 1 feeds: nothing enters it from the other side, and same-side entries keep the gap the two had in their own lane. E enters lane 1, which lane 2 also feeds. The exchange is not commanded while (a) any lane-2 vehicle ahead of E (front at or ahead of E's) would, in lane 1, fail the forced guard as E's leader — every such vehicle counts, driven or not, since an undriven vehicle's change cannot be read in advance (probe 4) — or (b) a driven exiter in lane 2 behind E would, in lane 1, fail the forced guard with E as its leader (its own mode-256 change executes after E's). An undriven vehicle behind E is executed after E by its own model, whose safety check sees E.

*Bounded, no chain.* Nobody but the pair is commanded; nothing is held (the exchange is a one-step request, the acceptance's); each vehicle is in one pair at most, entrants nearest the section end paired first; the pair is re-read every step and exists only while the geometry does; on the step of an exchange neither vehicle carries a speed target in any role (the cooperation's and easing's targets were for the two lanes it leaves). The pairs commanded are counted in `n_swaps` — the **40th `weave_sections` key** (docs/CONTRACTS.md §2, `WeaveSectionDiagnosticsOut`, `WEAVE_FIELDS`); the blocked pair-steps, the refusals by condition and each exchange's outcome on the next step (both changed, one, none) are state for a harness.

*The speed-differential pairing (task (b)), derived and measured as a harness form.* A pair at parity refused on the offset needs the rear to fall `D − d` farther behind (from fronts level, `len_P + D`); the front cannot be commanded faster (a target above its model is inert, `_weave_command`), so the rear drops back. From fronts level at `b` 1.67 m/s² the 10 m take 3.46 s and end 5.8 m/s slower — at the 5 m/s of the corridor's pairs, a stop. Form D (`FS_WP64_VAR=drop`): the rear of a pair refused on the offset alone is given a one-step target, IDM towards a virtual leader at P's rear moved back by `D − s0_R` (through `_weave_command`, clipped at `−b_R`, only below its own model and below any other target that step), never while it is below the creep speed, lapsing for a pair after `√(2 · (D − d₀)/b_R)` plus `pair_release_s` from its first refused step. The existing easing already does most of this: on the offset-refused pair-steps of the rule's runs the rear is already given a speed target by the other rules on 469 of 677 (69 %) at seed 3 and 798 of 1,197 (67 %) at seed 5, and the front on 230 (34 %) and 418 (35 %) — the front's closing the offset the rear opens.

**Measured.** Session harness `wp64_harness.py` (WP-62's, with `wp64_patch.py`: the swap's state counts and per-pair log in each row, a shadow census that runs the pair detection at the default with its commands discarded, and the harness forms), grid script `grid64.sh` (the same 29 runs as WP-51..62: seeds 3 / 4 / 5 on the Ruth St module at both demand points and both fleets, the Ruth St corridor fleet at the 271.4 m window, the T.H.52 corridor-demand and capacity fixtures, the two two-entrance fixtures, the moderate fixture, the golden; 20 simulated minutes at step 0.5 s, macOS, one grid at a time), and `wp64_corr.py`: the corridor section test's body with the key set in a copy of its call (the strict marker untouched), at seeds 3 / 4 / 5, with WP-61/62's readings. Forms: `off`, the default; **the rule** (`swap_pairs` = 1); S (harness), the sequenced exchange — of each pair the rule commands only the front vehicle changes in that step, the rear left to the section's ordinary acceptance on the next, once the front has left its target lane; D (harness), the rule with the rear's drop-back above; X (harness), conditions (ii)–(iii) read by the forced guard alone instead of the full acceptance — the upper bound of the rule family, every non-overlapping blocked pair whose lanes clear the weave's minimum. The census's list is module-level and the corridor script runs its seeds in one process, so seed 5's census was re-run in a process of its own (the first row had summed seeds 4 and 5); every other count is per run.
